subject: CloudNav vendor onboarding and PO pathways for AWS/Azure/GCP marketplaces
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily@cloudnav.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CloudNav vendor onboarding and PO pathways for AWS/Azure/GCP marketplaces

Hi Emily —

Great to meet earlier this week. As discussed, we're lining up the procurement path so CloudNav can be listed and transactable via the three cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, GCP). To keep it actionable, I pulled together the checklist and the minimal PO flow we expect from our typical mid-market customers. Attached is our marketplace onboarding checklist (PDF).

Quick summary / asks from CloudNav:
- Confirm you have an active vendor account on AWS Marketplace (AMSA profile) / equivalent for Azure and GCP, or whether you need Redwood to sponsor an initial listing.
- Send the company W-9 (or W-8BEN for non-US entity) and marketplace vendor intake form (we'll attach our preferred template).
- Confirm billing remit and invoicing cadence (Net 30 is typical; some customers require PO-first workflows).
- Fill in the PO template if ClientCorp (example customer) will require a PO before first invoice.

Next steps I propose:
1) You send vendor legal + tax docs to procurement@redwood.com and reply-all with confirmation.
2) We open a HubSpot deal and attach the marketplace listing task to our Partner Ops team.
3) Once tax/bank info is in place, we'll route a DocuSign PO (if required by the buyer) and onboard you to our Dedicated seller portal for metrics.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-min ops call next week to run through AWS-specific items (AMSA, pricing SKU mapping) and Azure/GCP differences — we find that a short alignment prevents rework.

Attachments referenced:
- redwood-marketplace-onboarding-checklist.pdf (attached)
- PO_Template_ClientCorp.docx (attached)

Thanks —
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

From: Emily Chen <emily@cloudnav.com>

Subject: Re: CloudNav vendor onboarding and PO pathways for AWS/Azure/GCP marketplaces

Thanks, Sergio —

Appreciate the clear checklist. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) Vendor accounts: CloudNav has active vendor profiles on AWS and GCP, but Azure is pending (we started the supplier validation last month and are waiting on the publisher agreement). If Redwood can provide a short checklist of the exact docs Azure wants, that would speed it up.

2) Tax docs: attached my company W-9 (CloudNav_vendor_W-9.pdf) and our completed marketplace intake (Marketplace_Vendor_Form_CloudNav.docx). Let me know if you need a legal-signed version versus my CFO-signed scanned copy.

3) PO flow: We typically accept PO-first for enterprise buyers. For the ClientCorp pilot you referenced, procurement@clientcorp.com requires a signed PO before provisioning. We can accept DocuSign POs.

4) Invoicing: Our billing team prefers monthly invoices with Net 30. If Redwood needs us to submit tax info into an AMSA console, point us to the guide.

I can join a 30-min ops call next Tue (13th) 10-10:30 PT. Laura / Karthik — are you available to walk the marketplace mapping then?

Attachments included: CloudNav_vendor_W-9.pdf; Marketplace_Vendor_Form_CloudNav.docx

Best,
Emily Chen
Head of Partnerships
CloudNav Solutions
emily@cloudnav.com | +1 (650) 888-0220

- Redwood Finance (cc Karthik): I'll loop you on the PO requirement for ClientCorp. Karthik, please confirm if Redwood can accept DocuSign-signed POs and whether we need the PO number present on the invoice to satisfy AR workflows.
